about: Grand-Puy-Lacoste is a Fifth Growth of the 1855 Classification, set on one of the gravel hills, or “puys,” that rise behind the town of Pauillac. Vines have grown here since the 1500s; the Lacoste family, who gave the estate its name, held it from the early 1700s into the late 1800s. Raymond Dupin owned it from 1932 until 1978, when it passed to the Borie family. François-Xavier Borie has made the wine since the 1979 vintage, and today runs the estate with his children, Emeline and Pierre-Antoine.

The vineyard lies in a single block around the château on very deep, coarse gravel over limestone, planted mostly to Cabernet Sauvignon with Merlot and a little Cabernet Franc, at 10,000 vines per hectare. In 2018, a ripe, generous Bordeaux vintage, the grapes were picked by hand between September 21 and October 5 and sorted twice, before and after destemming. After about three weeks of maceration, the wine aged 16 to 18 months in French oak barrels, roughly three quarters of them new.

The 2018 marked forty years of the Borie family at the estate, and critics received it as one of the château’s finest modern wines. The estate describes ripe black fruit and licorice on the nose, lifted by freshness and a mineral edge, and a precise, dense palate that balances power with elegance before a long, firmly structured finish. It is a Pauillac built for the cellar, though its ripe fruit already makes it generous at the table.
